waypoints.name: Manali
waypoints.advice: Manali is where the day begins. Next is Atal Tunnel north portal.

waypoints.name: Sarchu

sections.advice: Manali → Atal Tunnel north portal is 23 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Atal Tunnel north portal → Baralacha La climbs about 4890 m in 56 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Baralacha La → Sarchu drops about 4890 m over 38 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Leh–Manali Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: For 45 km this is Leh–Manali Highway, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Atal Tunnel north portal → Baralacha La
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 8.8%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.

scenicChapters.title: Manali-Leh Highway
scenicChapters.narrative: 4890 m come off over 74 km at around 13.0%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it — brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

leh-manali-highway-manali-sarchu.story: A one-way ride of 230 km, Manāli to the finish - roughly 3 h 10 in the saddle. On the way it passes Atal Tunnel north portal and Baralacha La. The highest point is about 5,100 m. Baralacha La is open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.

scenicChapters.title: Villa Zeno → Venice and its Lagoon
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 51 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
